event: Celsius Holdings / PepsiCo Distribution Partnership Conference Call
rows: Celsius Holdings / PepsiCo Distribution Partnership Conference Call ($550M PepsiCo Investment)
5% (quarterly, cash or in kind at Celsius option)
International market entry (UK, Germany, Canada, W. Europe)
Not depleted within ~6-7 months; multi-year purchases compressed to ~2 years
Transformational long-term distribution agreement: PepsiCo becomes Celsius's preferred US distribution partner, paired with a $550M convertible preferred investment.
Deal consolidates a fragmented network of 250+ independent regional distributors into a single best-in-class national DSD network with global expansion optionality.
Partnership grants access to new consumption occasions: food service, independent convenience, vending, college campuses, concessions, and the military.
The equity investment is structured to align incentives and give PepsiCo 'skin in the game'; Celsius was already cash-flow positive and self-funding.
Termination of existing distributor agreements is cash neutral to Celsius (separate funding covers buyouts), but charges must be recognized in Q3 2022 financials - numbers still being worked.
Termination fees and transaction costs will be called out separately for apples-to-apples comparability; PepsiCo's assistance is recorded to the balance sheet and amortized.
$550M preferred sits in mezzanine equity (above common, below liabilities); 5% dividend flows through the cash flow statement; near-term margin impact characterized as 'more or less neutral'.
Use of proceeds: accelerated cooler/vending rollouts (coolers pay back in ~4 months), sales/marketing/R&D, fleet expansion, sales force growth, international expansion, and M&A optionality.
Distribution transitions 'very rarely go smoothly' - Celsius is being strategic, leveraging team members (incl. Tony Guilfoyle) with prior PepsiCo-system transition experience and a built roadmap.
PepsiCo can grow its ownership over time beyond the current ~8.5% stake (not necessarily as preferred); no deep restrictions on a larger stake.
Celsius will be the exclusive healthy functional energy drink in PepsiCo's portfolio for an initial 24 months, with specific annual jointly-agreed KPIs (distribution, ACV, deliveries) as protection.
No access fee paid to PepsiCo - framed as a 'true partnership'; supply-chain/vertical-integration synergies exist but are not yet earmarked.
Co-packing strategy unchanged - PepsiCo cannot pack Celsius's product today, so Celsius continues using and expanding its existing co-pack network.
The deal is a North America agreement; international opportunities (PepsiCo distributes across many global markets) will be structured separately.
Real distribution gains expected in the back half of Q4 2022 into Q1 2023 when retailer resets take place; the team has already held 2023 review meetings with key retailers.
Quiet period ahead of the August 9, 2022 Q2 earnings call limited questions strictly to the PepsiCo distribution/investment agreement.
How will Celsius avoid losing brand momentum during a distribution changeover, given transitions rarely go smoothly?
Being extremely strategic; built a roadmap with PepsiCo and team members (incl. Tony Guilfoyle) experienced with prior PepsiCo-system transitions; monitoring extremely closely.
Rough idea of how much the distributor termination agreements will cost / how much of the $550M they consume?
The termination process is cash neutral to Celsius but will likely be recognized in Q3 2022 financial statements; numbers still being worked.
Why is M&A a use of proceeds, and why is the convertible preferred structure right given Celsius could self-fund from free cash flow?

M&A provides nimbleness though core portfolio remains the focus; despite being cash-flow positive, having PepsiCo take a meaningful stake aligns incentives ('skin in the game'); wrapping investment and distribution agreement together ensures alignment.
How quickly will the $550M be deployed, and what does it imply for US and international growth?

Will not rush; capital compresses multi-year cooler/vending purchases into ~2 years, funds supply-chain/vertical-integration evaluation and inventory build ahead of launch; $550M will not be depleted in 6-7 months.
How does the deal accelerate topline growth - distribution gains, velocity, targeted market share?

Anticipates ~40% increase in distribution expansion over the next 12 months, with major opportunities in college campuses and food service; must stay focused on the transition over the next 90-120 days.
Timeline for the international opportunity and initial markets; what does 'substantial margin accretion' look like and how quickly are cost savings realized?

International expansion into UK, Germany, Canada, Western Europe over the next 24-48 months (distribution gains ~24 months in); margin commentary kept high-level (quiet period) - cited simplification from 250 distributors to one, streamlining and CapEx assistance.
Can PepsiCo own more of Celsius, is Celsius the exclusive non-PepsiCo-owned energy drink, and how is 'healthy tension' avoided?

PepsiCo can grow its ownership over time; Celsius will be the exclusive healthy functional energy drink in PepsiCo's portfolio, filling a major gap, with enough contractual protections and aligned interests.
Are there criteria/timelines for future ownership, can PepsiCo produce/procure raw materials, and is Celsius paying an access fee?
No access fee - a 'true partnership'; no structural requirement for investment over time; supply-chain/vertical-integration synergies exist but are not yet earmarked.
Deal timing & PepsiCo brand prioritization risk
Why do the deal now, and what gives comfort PepsiCo will not prioritize its own brands over Celsius?

Celsius was not actively seeking a partner - the opportunity arose; protections include a 24-month healthy-functional-energy exclusivity, specific annual jointly-agreed KPIs, and the equity investment.
PepsiCo stake increase mechanics & vertical integration / co-packing
Can PepsiCo increase its stake (and what is the maximum), and will PepsiCo co-pack Celsius products?

Additional investment questions best directed to PepsiCo, but opportunities exist; global procurement evaluated as Celsius expands; PepsiCo cannot pack Celsius's product today, so Celsius continues using/expanding its existing co-pack network; deal is North America only.
KPI magnitude, co-packing changes & prior partnership lessons
Order of magnitude on the agreement's KPIs, co-packing changes, and lessons from the failed prior ('bank') partnership?

Declined KPI specifics (they range from distribution to ACV to deliveries, jointly agreed); no immediate co-packing changes; declined specific comment on the prior partnership, attributing issues more to product availability than operational execution.
How long will the 250-distributor transition take, will any remain, and why is the termination cash neutral?

Majority of distributors transitioned to the PepsiCo system by year-end with a few remaining in the legacy system; cash neutral because separate funding (outside the $550M growth capital) covers buyouts/transitional costs.
Are shelf resets a 2023 event or are some gains expected before year-end?
Initial selling into the PepsiCo system in Q3, with the bulk of distribution migrating end of Q3 into Q4; the real gain comes in the back half of Q4 into Q1 2023 when resets take place.
Accounting treatment of charges & near-term margin impact
Will there be unusual charges over the balance of the year, and is there a near-term negative margin hit?

Termination fees and transaction costs called out separately for apples-to-apples comparison; termination fee booked in full while PepsiCo's assistance is recorded to the balance sheet and amortized; preferred sits in mezzanine equity with dividends through the cash flow statement; near-term margin impact 'more or less neutral'.
